route: The Monk - West Cracks - Right Crack
face: The Monk — West Cracks, lower left side of the South Face
overview: A short 1-2 pitch companion line to the Left Crack, climbing the right-hand crack on the left side of The Monk's South Face with the crux up high.
A longer, harder alpine rock line up Cathedral Rock's northeast side; a 2003 direct-start/finish variation to the original buttress line is a sustained 5.9, 6-pitch, Grade III climb.

A class 3 gully on Cathedral Rock's northwest side, used as an alternate ascent line and, by some parties, as a descent back toward Peggy's Pond.
A 5.6-rated chimney line up Cathedral Rock's southeast face — a harder, less-traveled technical alternative to the class 3-4 Southwest Face scramble.

face: North Ridge (Chair) to the Bryant col/ridge crest
overview: An alpine ridge linkup that starts on Chair Peak's north ridge and follows the crest toward Bryant Peak, with parties often extending the traverse further to The Tooth or even Denny Mountain for a longer high-route day.
A moderate 3rd-to-low-5th-class rock line directly up the east face to the summit, one of the more accessible summer scrambling/climbing routes on the peak, with a well-known overhanging band crux.

A longer, sustained 5.7 ridge climb on Chair Peak, following the crest over false summits with a mix of solid and notably loose rock — the longest documented rock route on the peak by pitch count.

A modern 8-pitch sport-oriented rock line up the right side of the East Face, established in 2022 — the longest fully-pitched rock route documented on Chair Peak, finishing with a short scramble to the summit.

A more remote, adventurous alpine rock line up Chair Peak's west side, climbing a narrow entrance couloir to the ridge crest and then following the West Ridge to the summit — less traveled and more exposed than the Northeast Buttress.

face: Southwest Basin / Southwest Face, finishing on the SE side of the summit block
overview: The peak's shortest and most direct line: a long valley approach up the White River and Thunder Creek to a high camp in Chalangin Basin, followed by a snow/scramble climb up the open south slope and southwest face, through a short cliff band, to the summit.

overview: The original 1952 first-ascent line up Chianti Spire, gained by rappelling into the Burgundy-Chianti notch and climbing the peak's north side on then-loose rock; now rarely repeated in favor of the East Face/Rebel Yell.

face: West face — Let it Burn's line low, new ground through the middle, West Face's upper roof and chimney
overview: Accendo Lunae (Latin for 'Burning Moon'/'Illuminating Moon') is a West Face variation named partly in homage to Let it Burn and partly because the first ascent finished by moonlight. Established by Blake Herrington, Scott Bennett, and Graham Zimmerman in 2012.

route: Colchuck Balanced Rock Col (East Lake Side Approch)
overview: A scenic, non-technical approach/scramble route to the col between Colchuck Balanced Rock and Colchuck Peak, used both as an approach for the harder rock routes and as a moderate objective in its own right. The line is rated 3rd class overall (Grade II).

The free version of the Tempest Wall's aid line, Full Tilt starts several hundred feet down the gully to the right of the West Face's start and climbs about 1,200 ft over 5 pitches with excellent climbing from 5.9 to 5.11 and one pitch of 5.12.

face: West face, far right-hand end of the wall
overview: A 5-pitch, Grade III 5.10a/b trad route established by Tom Ramier, Abe Traven, and Craig Rankin — one of the more moderate multipitch options on the formation.
